title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
key_facts: A flaw in Linux's vhost subsystem (CVE-2026-74580, named Vghost) lets a local user read and write kernel memory and become root, across kernels from 4.11 to 7.2-rc4.
In one virtualisation setup an untrusted guest virtual machine can write to the host's memory and take over the QEMU process.
Tencent Zhuque Lab found it with its multi-agent AI system Corvus AI; the fix was released 3 Aug and the full write-up published 12 Oct.
No public sign it has been exploited yet.
Tencent reproduced the root chain on Ubuntu 26.04, RHEL 9.8, Amazon Linux 2023, Azure Linux 3.0 and Oracle Linux 10.2.
Red Hat, Amazon and Oracle Linux have shipped fixes; Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 kernels were still in progress as of 13 Oct.
Raters differ: kernel.org CVE team 8.8, Red Hat 7.3, Amazon 7.8, Oracle 7.3.
quote_evidence: The bug was found with help from Corvus AI, a multi-agent system Tencent built for kernel vulnerability research.
This is machine-assisted research, not an attack run by AI.
why_it_matters_hint: A nine-year-old flaw in widely used server software was found by AI, and patches are still arriving.
notes: Disclosure write-up was 12 Oct, two days before the window; first coverage in this window. Severity ratings differ between raters.
